limits: Python and libraries on this page: the examples run in your browser, in Python 3.13.2 with schedule 1.2.2, pyperclip 1.11.0, playsound3 3.3.2 and the time zone database tzdata 2026.5 (the versions the research ran, embedded as wheels), while the research ran Python 3.14.6 on Linux. Each concept example and each chapter example was run in the browser and compared with its recorded result.

Recorded, not run: 31 examples need something a browser's Python cannot give (another program, a shell, a thread, a real timer, the signals of an operating system, the process time zone, a system zone, a web browser program or the C library of Linux) or word an error, a warning or a method as Python 3.14 does and Python 3.13 does not, and one that takes about six seconds in a browser; each is shown with its output recorded under Python 3.14.6, labelled 'Recorded, not run on this page', with its reason: AppendixBAnswers, ArgumentList, AsyncioCallLater, CaptureOutput, CheckAndTimeout, ClipboardAndSound, ClockInfoTable, DatetimeObject, ExitCodes, FromTimestampZones, OpenCommand, PollingLoops, PopenNoWait, PosixFormula, ProfilingByClock, PstVersusPdt, RunWaits, ShellInjection, ShellTrueList, SleepAndSignals, SleepFunction, StrftimeFormat, StrptimeParse, SystemdCalendar, TerminateVsKill, TimerThread, UtcnowDeprecated, Webbrowser, Year2038, YearlessParsing, ZoneInfoZones.

Clock-dependent results are never shown as live: the examples that run use a fixed moment, a fixed zone or a stand-in clock (called EMULATED where the book's loop is run against it), and print values that do not depend on the day they are run. What the book's own statements print when they read the real clock (time.time(), time.ctime(), datetime.now()) differs from the book on every run, by design; the research recorded where each block differs.

The four libraries: playsound3-3.3.2-py3-none-any.whl, pyperclip-1.11.0-py3-none-any.whl, schedule-1.2.2-py3-none-any.whl, tzdata-2026.5-py2.py3-none-any.whl are embedded as the PyPI wheels, unchanged, and unpacked in the browser; their licences are Apache-2.0, BSD, MIT License (recorded in 03-materials/ch19/assets/ASSETS_PROVENANCE_v1_0_0.md). No file of the book's online materials (a zip of 7,759,877 bytes) is on this page.

NOT EXECUTED: a Windows computer (calc.exe, notepad, mspaint, the start command, Task Scheduler and schtasks), a Mac (the open command for an application, launchd and launchctl), a systemd timer (PID 1 here is not systemd; systemd-analyze only normalised expressions), a desktop session in which xdg-open or a browser could open anything, the sound (no audio device) and a clipboard program, the names of months and days in a locale other than C, Python 3.14.7, 3.14.8 and the final 3.15.0 (uv offered only 3.15.0b4), the commit the course pins, and the ping to nostarch.com (the container's network lost the packets).

MEASURED, single runs on the machine of the day, not results of a program on this page: loop 2.450 s, math.prod 2.372 s, math.factorial 0.0969 s; wall time of the run: 60.037 s for 60 sleeps of one second.

What the public sites answered on 2026-10-13 is in live_observations_v1_0_0.json: the chapter's page (status 200, 88,909 bytes, equal to the digest in the book's ontology), the newest PyPI releases (tzdata 2026.5, playsound3 3.3.2, pyperclip 1.11.0) and the pages of the stories; cron 3.0pl1 was installed and run for real on the machine of the study (first record 24.1 seconds after the crontab was installed).

One program was run under 11 interpreters (3.11.17, 3.12.3, 3.13.16, 3.14.0, 3.14.1, 3.14.2, 3.14.3, 3.14.4, 3.14.5, 3.14.6, 3.15.0b4) with the same package versions; the 11 items that differ between them are listed in interpreter_record_v1_0_0.json (for example the wording of date and time errors, date.strptime, which Python 3.14 added, and the warning for a month and day without a year). The book's Appendix A pins playsound3 2.4.0, and the chapter's statements were also replayed with that version.
